run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T07:43:11Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by a chaos-mesh network-delay experiment applied to the product-catalog pod. From 07:41:10Z through at least 07:49:10Z, the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay spawned a NetworkChaos object every minute (…-jj42n, …-6rtdg, …-bx27q, …-x5l64, …-b5dxg, …-gjgf2, …-d9vpw, …-26dqc, …-hcwrz), each 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9' and recovered after ~55s. Exactly in that period frontend-proxy ingress spans turned to errors (0/min through 07:42, then 272, 248, 272, 256, 262, 254, 268, 260 error spans per minute), 1115 of ~1999 ingress spans in the last 15m were STATUS_CODE_ERROR, mostly HTTP 504 at ~15.00s (frontend-proxy's upstream timeout), and frontend calls to check out failed with 500 / gRPC 13 'failed to prepare order: failed to get product'. The direct failure at the dependency is visible on checkout: its oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct spans fail with gRPC 14 'error reading from server: read tcp 100.96.4.114:59432->100.64.188.136:8080: read: connection reset by peer' after 8.4–20.0s. Product-catalog itself stayed up (pod Running/Ready, 0 restarts, no error log lines, zero spans slower than 5s), while its inbound traffic collapsed (server GetProduct 12,994.7 per 20m before vs 93.7 per 15m during; ListProducts 1070.5 before vs 0 during; frontend's client GetProduct calls 11,588 per 20m before vs 0 during) — i.e. the delay/loss is on the pod's network path, not in its application. The frontend-proxy is therefore the symptom carrier (504 upstream timeouts) and product-catalog's network chaos is the origin. A separate OOMKill of the fraud-detection pod at 07:37:25Z is unrelated to this alert (no error/slow spans on its operations).

claims.text: frontend-proxy ingress spans carried 1115.3 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans and 883.6 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans in the 15 minutes ending 07:58:25Z; the error spans are on the 'ingress' operation, while 'router frontend egress' had only 22.1 error spans.

frontend-proxy ingress error spans were 0 per minute through 07:42Z and then 272, 248, 272, 256, 262, 254, 268 and 260 per minute for the points 07:43–07:50Z, so the error signal began between 07:40Z and 07:43Z and stayed at ~250–272 error spans/min.

The failing frontend-proxy spans are HTTP 504 responses with duration ~15.00s: ingress spans of 15000895/15000669/15000611/15000228/14999803 µs with status tags error=true, http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR, each parented by a 'router frontend egress' span of ~15.00s with error="true" and http.status_code="0" (no upstream response), whose child frontend 'GET' span ran ~15.000s and returned http.status_code 200.

In the last 15 minutes the only services with error spans were frontend-proxy (1137.4), frontend (292.6), recommendation (1.05, all on /flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream) and 0 for payment, cart, fraud-detection, accounting and ad; frontend's error spans are grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (55.8), POST /api/checkout (102.0), executing api route (pages) /api/checkout (102.2), GET (22.1) and POST (10.5).

The checkout failures trace to the product-catalog dependency: frontend's 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' spans error with rpc.grpc.status_code=13 and message '13 INTERNAL: failed to prepare order: failed to get product #"1YMWWN1N4O"', the checkout 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' span errors with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and otel.status_description 'error reading from server: read tcp 100.96.4.114:59432->100.64.188.136:8080: read: connection reset by peer' after 20.0s, and frontend 'POST /api/checkout' returns 500.

Traffic to product-catalog collapsed during the error burst: product-catalog server span oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct fell from 12994.7 calls in the 20 minutes 07:20–07:40Z to 93.7 calls in the 15 minutes ending 07:58:25Z, and ListProducts from 1070.5 to 0; checkout's oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct client spans fell from 1385.3 per 20m to 86.4 per 15m.

The frontend is a heavy caller of product-catalog and its calls stopped completing: frontend span grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct increased 11588.4 over the 20 minutes 07:20–07:40Z but 0 over the 15 minutes ending 07:58:25Z, while in that same window frontend recorded 1555.6 successful-status GET spans and 1011.1 GET spans slower than 5s.

A chaos-mesh Schedule named otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay in namespace chaos-mesh spawned 9 NetworkChaos objects ('Create new object: otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay-jj42n' at 07:41:10Z, then -6rtdg 07:42:10Z, -bx27q 07:43:10Z, -x5l64 07:44:10Z, -b5dxg 07:45:10Z, -gjgf2 07:46:10Z, -d9vpw 07:47:10Z, -26dqc 07:48:10Z, -hcwrz 07:49:10Z).

Each NetworkChaos event reports 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9' about 55 seconds before its 'Time up according to the duration' and 'Successfully recover chaos for otel-demo/product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9' (e.g. -jj42n applied 07:41:10Z, recovered 07:42:05Z; -hcwrz applied 07:49:10Z), and PodNetworkChaos events name the same pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9; the only chaos involved-object kinds in the window are NetworkChaos/Schedule/PodNetworkChaos, all pointing at this one pod.

product-catalog's own application was not the slow component: pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9 is Running and Ready with 0 restarts, started 07:05:18Z on node i-0b2137ceca968ac10, has no previous container instance, and its container logs in 07:40–07:48Z contain only 'Product Found', 'Reloading Product Catalog...' and 'Loaded 10 products' with zero lines matching err/error/fatal/fail/panic/timeout/reset.

The product-catalog container's pod IP is 100.96.4.247, and the checkout pod that reported the reset is 100.96.4.114 (matching the '100.96.4.114:59432->100.64.188.136:8080' reset source), i.e. the reset was observed on a connection from the checkout pod toward the product-catalog service address.

Spans slower than 5s were observed only for frontend (GET 1011.1, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 93.7, POST 100.9, executing api route /api/checkout 97.9, POST /api/checkout 97.8), checkout (about 80–112 per 5m) and frontend-proxy (about 443–1456 per 5m) during the burst, while product-catalog, cart, currency, payment, shipping, quote, email and image-provider each had 0 spans slower than 5s.

The flagd fault-injection ConfigMap in otel-demo (flagd-config/demo.flagd.json) currently has every fault flag at defaultVariant "off", including productCatalogFailure, paymentFailure, adFailure, cartFailure and recommendationCacheFailure.

Pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-n7vmf restarted twice and its previous container instance terminated with reason OOMKilled, exit code 137, finishedAt 2026-11-17T07:37:25Z; in the incident's error window fraud-detection had 0 error spans and 0 spans slower than 5s.

The ~15s frontend page GET spans behind the frontend-proxy 504s are caused by the same product-catalog network delay: the frontend's grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct calls dropped from 11588.4 per 20m to 0 while product-catalog received almost no GetProduct/ListProducts calls, so page renders blocked on calls that never completed; the sampled page-GET traces themselves show no product-catalog child span, so this link is inferred from timing and traffic collapse rather than a visible call edge.

Flag-based fault injection (e.g. productCatalogFailure) is not the cause: all flagd-config flags are at defaultVariant off, product-catalog logged no application errors, and the observed failure mode is connection reset/timeout toward the pod rather than a product-specific application error.

A product-catalog crash, restart or resource kill is not the cause: the pod shows 0 container restarts, no previous container instance, a Running/Ready status and no OOMKilled or Evicted marker, and its own spans stayed under 5s.

The fraud-detection OOMKill at 07:37:25Z is not the cause of this alert: it is a different pod, its service shows 0 error spans and 0 slow spans in the alert window, and its failure precedes the frontend-proxy error burst (which started between 07:40Z and 07:43Z).

frontend-proxy itself is not the origin: its failing spans are HTTP 504 gateway timeouts with a ~15.00s egress span carrying http.status_code="0", i.e. it timed out waiting for frontend, whose GET span ran ~15.000s; no frontend-proxy restart or pod fault was observed.

Cart, payment, accounting and ad each had 0 error spans in the alert window, and cart, currency, email, shipping, quote, payment, image-provider, accounting and ad each had 0 spans slower than 5s, so no other otel-demo workload shows its own failure evidence tied to this incident.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not loaded in the queried Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules for rule_name RequestErrorRate returned no_data), so the alert's expression and its reported 'current: 1.422222222222222' could not be reproduced or verified; also no http_* or app_* metric series (e.g. http_server_request_duration_seconds_count) exist in this Prometheus, only traces_span_metrics_* and app_payment_transactions_total-style series.

NetworkChaos and Schedule objects are not readable with the available Kubernetes resource kinds; therefore the delay value, direction, correlation/loss settings and the experiment's selector definition could not be read, and no NetworkChaos/Schedule object status can be cited beyond their events.

Telemetry in this run ends at ~07:50Z (Jaeger's newest returned spans start 07:50:10Z, several metric views report data_as_of 07:50:00Z, observed at ~08:00Z), so whether the chaos Schedule kept firing after 07:49:10Z and whether the error burst continued past ~07:50Z are unknown.
No frontend-pod application log lines were retrievable for 07:40–07:58Z (fetch_pod_logs read 0 bytes / no_data), so the frontend's own view of the 15s render stalls could not be confirmed from logs.
kafka, postgresql, valkey-cart, flagd, otel-collector and load-generator were not verified for health in this investigation; load-generator only appears as the client reporting 504/500 responses.

Cluster events in namespace data-recorders (Job Completed/SuccessfulCreate, PVC provisioning, Deployment ScalingReplicaSet, StatefulSet and ReplicaSet creation, plus a PersistentVolume VolumeFailedDelete event) are unexplained by this evidence and were not tied to the otel-demo impact; they remain an uninvestigated change in the window.
Whether any chaos experiments ran against otel-demo before 07:41:10Z cannot be established from the retained events (they start 07:24:03Z) or from the unreadable chaos CRs.
next_steps: Ask the chaos engineering owner to confirm the otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay schedule's spec (delay, jitter, correlation, loss, direction, duration) and whether it is still scheduled; correlate its lifecycle with any extension of the frontend-proxy error burst after 07:50Z.

Check the Alertmanager/Prometheus rule set that defines RequestErrorRate to confirm which series and window produce the reported value 1.4222, and verify the alert clears once the product-catalog network chaos is stopped.

If the delay is intentional, consider temporarily pausing or excluding product-catalog from the chaos schedule and re-checking frontend-proxy ingress error rate and frontend page latency at that point to confirm the causal link.
Verify whether the frontend should have a shorter gRPC deadline to product-catalog so that a delayed dependency does not consume the full 15s proxy timeout and turn page requests into 504s.
